quiz_map.support: No single record is wrong, but the count is.
Data events are high-volume activities that CloudTrail does not log by default.
The event names are a list, and list items are joined with a logical OR.
A streaming invocation writes an AwsApiCall record and, when the stream finishes, a second record whose eventType is AwsServiceEvent.
A single global threshold of 400 sits above every maximum, so it would have produced no alerts in three weeks.
The ordered type requires in addition that the events appear in the order in which the rules are listed.
In KQL, the double equals operator is case-sensitive.
Sigma's tag list defines no namespace for MITRE ATLAS.
A block written as a map of field and value pairs matches only when all of its fields match.
For Bedrock the value is bedrock.amazonaws.com
It does not exclude the Delete call for anyone, and it does not exclude the role's other actions.
Who made the call, with which access key, from which address and client?
Is there a change ticket or a pipeline run at that time?
A rule that counts model invocations must keep only AwsApiCall, or every streamed call is counted twice and the rule fires at half the real volume.
A threshold belongs above the highest normal hour, with a margin, and low enough to catch abuse.
A threshold rule that fires on real, authorised activity has worked correctly.
Pellham's sequence uses temporal_ordered, groups by userIdentity.arn and uses a timespan of 1h.
In KQL the == operator is case-sensitive, so EventName == invokemodel finds no rows.
Test with known-bad and known-good samples.
Data events are not logged by default, and nobody had enabled them.
The access key ID that was used to sign the request

unverified.item: SPL base-search syntax in the lesson (sourcetype=..., field=value, parentheses with OR, a quoted value)
unverified.why: The Splunk search-command reference could not be fetched (help.splunk.com search page blocked by the fetch tool, docs.splunk.com returned 403). Only the stats command page and Splunk's own published Bedrock detection were read.
unverified.handled: softened to the minimal forms that Splunk's published detection uses (sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail, eventSource, eventName, stats count BY); the NOT exclusion with a wildcard and any time-bucketing command were left out

unverified.item: Zscaler web log key names and the category value AI and ML Applications
unverified.why: Zscaler's own NSS web-log format page returned an empty body to the fetch tool. Key names were read in Google SecOps and Elastic documentation that reproduce the feed template; the category name comes from a Zscaler blog dated May 2023 and Zscaler may have renamed or split it since.
unverified.handled: lesson tells the reader that the feed is a template and to check the category names in their own tenant; urlsupercategory, urlclass, appname, appclass and reason values were left out of the raw block
